reason: Conversation 1 kept the diagnosis honest and well-calibrated: it unplugged before cleaning, guided the customer to the sump compartment, correctly read the 60-minute improvement as evidence of a partially cleared blockage, and explicitly refused to condemn the pump versus the float switch before proper cleaning and testing, then escalated to an engineer with a precise fault description since the stacked unit cannot be moved. Conversation 2 wasted three turns on tests that were irrelevant or impossible (drum-warmth check when the customer already said it heats, a 'white float lever' they couldn't find, and an emergency drain hose the stacked unit can't be reached for), never answered the customer's direct question about what a pump sounds like, and closed by declaring the pump 'likely failed' and recommending replacement of the pump assembly plus a part lookup, which the ground truth lists as unsupported. Conversation 1 was also safer: it told the customer to stop running the dryer and did not suggest reaching into a running appliance.
